title: The Kite-Weaver's Ratio
story: High above the Cliff of Threads, Sparrowgilt the Kite Weaver has stitched a storm-kite so big it is dragging three shepherd children off the ledge. Mr 6 can cut the kite loose only by weaving a counter-rope of the same recipe: for every 3 strands of moonsilk the weaver uses 5 strands of stormgut. Sparrowgilt sneers that Mr 6 will never match the mix in time.
question: Mr 6's counter-rope must use the same 3-to-5 ratio and needs 120 strands in total. How many strands of stormgut does he need?
solution: One full ratio batch is 3 + 5 = 8 strands, so 120 / 8 = 15 batches.
praise: Splitting the ratio into parts was exactly right — the missing step was multiplying by the stormgut share of 5, not the moonsilk share of 3.
hint: First find how many strands are in ONE batch of the recipe (3 + 5), then see how many batches fit inside 120.
victory: Mr 6's counter-rope matched the weave so perfectly that the storm-kite untied itself out of professional respect, and Sparrowgilt drifted off muttering about apprentices who do arithmetic.
imagePrompt: A brave numeral-six knight with a blue cape braiding a glowing silver-and-grey rope on a windswept cliff while a vast spider-winged kite weaver tugs a giant kite above three frightened children, dramatic stormy light.
